data.name: EnergyChartNote
data.value: Power, averaged over each quarter hour that was observed — the store keeps energy, and a bucket the service only saw part of is divided by the part it saw, so a restart is a gap rather than a dip the sun never took. {0} is import above the line and export below it; {1} is charging above and discharging below. Click a name in the legend to take that series out. A bar along the bottom marks the windows that were only partly observed — the same ones the table below shows in italics.

data.name: EnergyTableNote
data.value: Every figure is kWh over that interval, in {0} time. Import and export are kept apart, and so are the battery's two directions — a net figure could not tell an idle quarter hour from a busy one that happened to balance. {1} is the residual of the others (the car included), not a separate measurement.

data.name: NoForecastHeld
data.value: No forecast is held yet. Either no Solcast account is configured for this installation, or nothing has been fetched since the controller started — {0} says which, and is where the account is entered. The forecast is refreshed on its own schedule in daylight; this page shows whatever was last fetched and never asks for one itself.

data.name: ForecastChartNote
data.value: Expected PV power against time, 30-minute periods, in {0} time. The line is {1} — the median, as likely to be beaten as missed — and the band behind it is {2}: the width of that gap is how sure the sky is, and it is the reason this is a picture rather than four numbers. The solid rule is the midnight between the two days; the dashed one is now. Click a name in the legend to take that series out.

data.name: NoRangeNote_0
data.value: Some periods carry no range of their own

data.name: NoRangeNote
data.value: {0} — the provider sent only a median for them, and the band collapses onto the line there. A band no wider than the line is not a promise; the table below shows a dash in those rows.

data.name: MorningMissing
data.value: {0} A forecast provider only ever answers what is still to come, so the controller can say what this morning was expected to bring only if it was running through it — and this one has nothing retained before then. The empty stretch on the left of the chart is a gap in what is known, not a dark morning.

data.name: NothingHeld
data.value: Nothing is held for this day.

data.name: ForecastTableNote
data.value: Power in W, energy in kWh, times in {0} time. Each row is the half hour it names, and every figure on it is the average power the provider expects across that half hour — so the energy column is simply that power over thirty minutes. The night rows are kept: a 0 W row at 02:00 {1} the forecast, and a table that drops rows is one you have to learn the rules of before you can trust a gap in it. A period is counted under the day it {2} on, which is how the dashboard and the day plan count it too, so each day opens with the half hour that ends at its own midnight. {3} — every refresh re-forecasts them until the day arrives.

data.name: ForecastHorizonNote
data.value: The horizon is about 48 hours, which is why this is two days and not a week. The dashboard's {0} table is the same two days in four numbers each.
